prerequisites: Proficiency in knowledge acquired from Physics and Mathematics courses taken in the degrees providing access to the engineering programs where this subject is taught.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Photons, light waves that behave like particles
assessment_rules: The final grade is the higher of two possibilities. Option A: 0.8 * Face-to-face exam + 0.15 * Continuous Assessment Tests + 0.05 * Laboratory practices. Option B: 0.95 * Face-to-face exam + 0.05 * Laboratory practices. Continuous assessment tests (PEC) are voluntary. It is mandatory to pass the laboratory practices to pass the course. The face-to-face exam normally consists of two problems (3 points each) and one theory question (4 points) chosen from two options.
